arm-A.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-A.summary: A phone reaches Neo's cubicle and Morpheus, on the line, warns that forces are closing in and will not say what they intend. Neo sees Agent Smith leading cops onto the floor and a female employee pointing out his cubicle, and he follows Morpheus's instructions out of the row and into an empty office. Morpheus directs him out to a ledge from which he can reach the roof; Neo commits, but his nerve breaks when the wind blasts him and the phone falls from his grip just as a cop opens the door, and he climbs back inside into the hands of the waiting cop. He is seized, handcuffed, and forced into a dark sedan in the Agents' custody. Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken and knows the extraction has failed.
arm-A.action: The event folds a raid, a guided escape, and a failed leap into one motion. Neo is converted from a recipient of messages into a fugitive and then into a prisoner: guided out of the cubicle, out to the window ledge, and back inside into Agent Smith's custody. Morpheus's remote guidance gets him out of the row but cannot steady his body at the ledge, and the dropped phone severs his only link to that guidance at the moment he most needs it. The one exit he could not bring himself to take is the only one that would have kept him free.

state_triples.reading: Neo is being tested at every level at once — his body betrays him, his self-image as an insignificant man who did nothing collides with a pursuit that treats him as the most wanted person in the building, and his terror of the ledge blinds him to the fact that capture is the worse fate. He follows Morpheus because the alternative is to stay and find out what 'they' will do, but the moment the choice becomes physical and solitary, the part of him that has always believed he is nobody wins, and he climbs back toward the danger he thinks is survivable. arm-B.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-B.summary: A softpak delivers a ringing phone to Neo's cubicle and Morpheus guides him through the raid, but the escape stalls at a window ledge and ends when the Agents take him into custody, which Trinity sees from outside.
arm-B.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that forces are closing in. Neo peeks over the partition and spots Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones guiding a cluster of officers, while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down he moves down the line until he reaches the first office on the left side. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken in her rearview mirror.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves from a man who can still duck and argue his way through a crisis to one whose body betrays him at the one moment that matters. He follows Morpheus precisely through the office and even forces himself onto the ledge, but the wind and the drop expose a conviction that none of this should be happening to someone as insignificant as he believes himself to be, and that self-conception — not the height — is what he cannot climb past. His retreat toward the office is a retreat toward the very custody that will do worse to him, which he cannot yet see.

arm-A.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-A.summary: A phone reaches Neo's cubicle and Morpheus, on the line, warns that forces are closing in and will not say what they intend. Neo sees Agent Smith leading cops onto the floor and a female employee pointing out his cubicle, and he follows Morpheus's instructions out of the row and into an empty office. Morpheus directs him out to a ledge from which he can reach the roof; Neo commits, but his nerve breaks when the wind blasts him and the phone falls from his grip just as a cop opens the door, and he climbs back inside into the hands of the waiting cop. He is seized, handcuffed, and forced into a dark sedan in the Agents' custody. Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken and knows the extraction has failed.
arm-A.action: The event folds a raid, a guided escape, and a failed leap into one motion. Neo is converted from a recipient of messages into a fugitive and then into a prisoner: guided out of the cubicle, out to the window ledge, and back inside into Agent Smith's custody. Morpheus's remote guidance gets him out of the row but cannot steady his body at the ledge, and the dropped phone severs his only link to that guidance at the moment he most needs it. The one exit he could not bring himself to take is the only one that would have kept him free.

state_triples.reading: Neo is being tested at every level at once — his body betrays him, his self-image as an insignificant man who did nothing collides with a pursuit that treats him as the most wanted person in the building, and his terror of the ledge blinds him to the fact that capture is the worse fate. He follows Morpheus because the alternative is to stay and find out what 'they' will do, but the moment the choice becomes physical and solitary, the part of him that has always believed he is nobody wins, and he climbs back toward the danger he thinks is survivable. arm-B.title: The Agents seize Neo at the office
arm-B.summary: A softpak delivers a ringing phone to Neo's cubicle and Morpheus guides him through the raid, but the escape stalls at a window ledge and ends when the Agents take him into custody, which Trinity sees from outside.
arm-B.action: A Federal Express Guy delivers a softpak to Neo at his cubicle; inside is a cellular phone that rings the moment Neo holds it, and Morpheus warns that forces are closing in. Neo peeks over the partition and spots Agent Smith, Agent Brown and Agent Jones guiding a cluster of officers, while a female employee points out his cubicle. Following Morpheus's commands, Neo lunges into the empty cubicle across the hall, hides in a corner while the Agents search his own, then rolls out and sneaks down he moves down the line until he reaches the first office on the left side. Alone in that office, he opens a window onto a scaffold and a ledge, argues that the climb is impossible, then commits and climbs out onto the ledge anyway; a blast of wind knocks him off balance, he drops the phone and watches it fall, and his nerve breaks so he climbs back inside just as a cop opens the door. Outside the skyscraper, the Agents lead a handcuffed Neo through the revolving doors and force him into a dark sedan while Trinity, watching from her motorcycle, sees him taken in her rearview mirror.

arm-A.title: Neo is reclaimed and taken to Morpheus
arm-A.summary: Waking from a nightmare that left him mouthless with a creature lodged in his abdomen, Neo is reached by a tapped phone on which Morpheus names him 'the One,' tells him Morpheus has spent his life searching for him, warns that the danger is himself, and wins his reluctant '... Yes' before hanging up. Trinity then pulls up beside him at The Adams Street bridge and gets him into a car, where Switch holds him at gunpoint and the crew means to run a steel-and-glass device on him. Neo tries to bolt, but Trinity's appeal to a road he already knows stops him, and he closes the car door and lets them take him on through the wet dark toward Morpheus — committing without trusting his captors.

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being named into a fate he never asked for. Each authority — the nightmare, Morpheus, Trinity — promises a future that demands surrender, and every time the promise lands on him as nausea rather than relief because it inverts his belief that he is 'nobody.' His '... Yes' is spoken from vertigo, not conviction, and his final act, closing the car door, is the same reflex dressed up as agency: he chooses the abyss he recognizes over the one he cannot see. He does not yet trust Trinity; he only trusts his own terror a bit

state_triples.reading: Neo moves through the event as a man being reclaimed by a destiny he never asked for and still cannot comprehend. Each surrender is framed — by Morpheus's prophecy, by Trinity's gentleness — as a choice, and he accepts the framing because the alternative (the road he knows, the abyss he has always been running toward) is more terrifying than compliance. He closes the door not out of trust but because staying feels marginally less like falling; the event's quiet horror is that his one act of 'agency' is the surrender of his agency.
